cultural.vision_reason: A fish-skin/leather quiver with fur and appliqué scroll-work decoration, a type of arms-related equipment consistent with Nanai (Amur region) material culture and craft style.

physical.title: quiver
physical.summary: A quiver, made of leather and fur and decorated with appliqué.  Long and rectangular, with a flap at the top.  Made in six sections, stitched together horizontally.  Decorated immediately below opening with square piece of appliqué cloth; flap covered with same.  Scroll shapes picked out with natural cream tabby linen cloth, against a blue (indigo dyed?) ground.  Outlining of motifs worked in green, yellow and blue cotton (?) yarns.  Small band of appliqué at bottom of quiver.  Fur appliqué used on remaining parts of front, much of it now disappeared.  Leather ties at sides and to fasten quiver at top.  Quite a lot of stitching has come undone; also holes.
